M.title: Sweep grace is measured from work creation rather than the last possible worker start
M.scenario: owner.lock mtime is set when WorkDirectory is constructed. Snapshotting and prepare happen afterward and have no total 300-second bound; even local regular-file copying, backpressure or a metadata-lock wait can consume that age before launch. If the supervisor then dies or returns unverified cleanup shortly after launching, the free lock is already older than SWEEP_AFTER_SECONDS and sweep_work deletes scratch while that newly started worker is still within its own runtime. A deterministic probe aged a held work lock to model long staging: sweep correctly skipped it while held, then removed it immediately on keep/close, leaving no grace from the recent abandonment. No real worker/process-kill run is claimed by this probe.
M.fix: Base sweep eligibility on the last possible launch/abandonment point or, preferably, retain the actual owned unit identity and verify termination before deletion. Persist a safe abandonment timestamp while ownership is held and account for launch/startup uncertainty, supervisor crash and clock behavior; a creation-time age is insufficient. Add long-staging-then-launch/abandon barrier coverage proving no sweep before the worker could have terminated.

M.status: CONFIRMED source lifecycle gap; injected cancellation probe
M.title: Cancellation bypasses scratch retention when unit cleanup cannot be verified
M.scenario: asyncio.CancelledError inherits BaseException and is not caught by except Exception around launch. The A4 cancellation path calls _abandon, whose final _verify_cleanup boolean is discarded, then propagates cancellation even if cleanup was not verified. PackageExportService therefore leaves WorkDirectory._removable=True and its finally removes scratch. A launch-injected CancelledError probe confirmed scratch was not marked kept and close deleted it. This violates the new retention guarantee for a worker that may still run; ordinary RuntimeError and unclean returned outcomes are correctly handled.
M.fix: Handle cancellation as a distinct interrupted-execution path: establish/propagate verified unit termination, or conservatively mark the work kept before re-raising cancellation. Preserve task cancellation semantics and allow the owning M7 recovery path to classify the interrupted attempt. Add a cancellation-during-worker test with failed cleanup verification, asserting scratch survives and no receipt or same-command rebuild occurs. Also bound and account for cancellation of thread-based work construction/snapshotting rather than assuming await cancellation terminates those operations.
